tweets.text: The demo stayed responsive the whole time. Buttons changed state without a glitch. Windows opened and closed without freezing. We stacked a few on top of each other and nothing stuttered. Video

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The stack it used: Three.js for the WebGL background, Tailwind served via a CDN, Font Awesome, two Google fonts, and vanilla JS for the rest. There was no no build step / bundler /framework used. We think this was a right call for a demo. Overall, the code looked clean and well-structured.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: There was also a command palette, a search bar that floats above the workspace with a list of quick actions. We could type a command or app name, or pick from the menu: open Terminal, Live Pulse, Streams, Code Carrier, or Neural Atlas. There was also Reset spatial view to snap windows back to default positions, and Close all floating windows to clear the workspace in one move. Let's analyze the source code. Video

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The result was a futuristic OS demo with multiple floating windows that lives inside the browser. Every window opened, closed, and dragged around the 3D space. Video

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: We used Kilo Code for VS Code and Agent Manager to interact with the model. The full prompt: "Create a full-screen interactive 3D browser demo of a futuristic operating system. Floating windows, command palettes, app cards, and data streams should exist in 3D space. Use smooth animations, parallax, reflections, and subtle soundless motion. Make it feel usable, not just decorative." Grok Build 0.1 produced the first working version in under two minutes, for seven cents, using less than a fifth of its context window. Let’s take a deeper look at the result.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Can Grok Build 0.1 do more than static landing pages? That was the question we kept getting after creating 5 one-shot landing page examples. So we threw the hardest interactivity prompt we could think of at it: build a 3D browser demo of a futuristic OS. Here is how it did: Video
